{
  "hook": "High-altitude Xinomavro from the Yianakohori vineyard defines this bottling, where limestone-rich soils and a cool Macedonian climate produce a structural profile often compared to Barolo. By selecting fruit from specific blocks with southern exposure, Kir-Yianni creates a wine that balances aggressive tannins with high natural acidity.",
  "wine_summary": "Ramnista is a benchmark for Naoussa, representing the modern evolution of the Xinomavro grape. Kir-Yianni, founded by Yiannis Boutaris, focuses on taming the variety's notoriously fierce phenolic structure through precise vineyard management and aging in French and American oak. This 100% Xinomavro is sourced from the estate's undulating hills, where the variation in slope and soil creates a wine of high aromatic complexity.\n\nThe wine matters because it proves that Greek indigenous varieties can produce long-lived, site-specific reds that compete with the great nebbiolo-based wines of the world. While many Naoussa producers struggled with consistency in the past, the recurring gold and silver medals from TEXSOM across the 2011-2015 vintages confirm that Ramnista is a reliable standard-bearer for the appellation.",
  "terroir_expression": "The Naoussa appellation is characterized by a Mediterranean climate with continental influences, but Ramnista specifically benefits from the clay-limestone soils of the Yianakohori estate. This calcium-rich geology contributes to the wine's 'salty' mineral finish and helps regulate the vine's water intake, while the 280-330m altitude ensures cool nights that preserve malic acid. The result is a palate defined by sun-dried tomato and olive tapenade notes, a direct sensory link to the scrubby, herbal landscape of northern Greece.",
  "vinification_summary": "Winemaking centers on managing Xinomavro’s high tannin—the polyphenolic compounds found in grape skins and seeds that provide grip—through a 12-to-15-month aging period in 225-liter and 500-liter oak barrels. The use of larger formats and 25% new wood prevents the oak from masking the grape's delicate floral and spice aromas. Malolactic fermentation, the process of converting sharp malic acid into softer lactic acid, is fully completed to round out the wine's naturally high-strung acidity.",
  "food_pairing": "Slow-roasted lamb shoulder with rosemary and garlic works because the wine's high acidity cuts through the fat while the tannins bind to the protein. For a casual pairing, try a lamb gyro with extra tzatziki; the cucumber and garlic in the sauce highlight the wine's herbal undertones. Smoked brisket with a vinegar-based North Carolina BBQ sauce provides a sharp counterpoint to the wine's dried fruit notes. In a fine dining setting, wild mushroom risotto with truffle oil complements the savory, earthy development found in older vintages like the 2013.",
  "comparable_wines": "Produttori del Barbaresco Torre — shares the same translucent color, high acidity, and firm tannic spine found in Xinomavro. Vietti Perbacco Nebbiolo delle Langhe — offers a similar balance of red fruit and savory earthiness at a near-identical price point. Domaine Sigalas Mavrotragano — another Greek high-acid red that emphasizes volcanic-style minerality and structural longevity.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied dry red with high acidity, assertive tannins, and savory tomato-leaf notes",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink now after decanting for two hours, or cellar for another 5-8 years to allow the tannins to soften into a silky texture.",
  "value_assessment": "$29.46 is an aggressive price for a wine that consistently earns gold medals and ages like a top-tier Piemontese red. It competes directly with entry-level Langhe Nebbiolo or mid-range Rioja Reserva, but offers significantly more structural depth and site-specificity than most $30 domestic Pinot Noirs. It is an essential purchase for collectors building a cellar on a budget.",
  "market_position": "Ramnista occupies the 'sommelier's secret' niche on restaurant lists, frequently appearing in trendy Mediterranean spots and wine bars focused on indigenous varieties. While it hasn't reached the mainstream recognition of Napa Cabernet, it is a staple for retail shops that cater to curious drinkers looking for high-acid, food-friendly alternatives to Pinot Noir. It is a 'buy by the case' wine for those who value structure over fruit-forward ripeness.",
  "insider_take": "The tradeoff with Ramnista is its uncompromising acidity; if you prefer plush, jammy reds like Zinfandel, you will find this wine painfully austere. It is a wine for the patient drinker who understands that Xinomavro is meant to be a savory experience rather than a fruit bomb. Skip this if you aren't serving it with food, as the tannins require protein to show their best side.",

parsed.hook: High-altitude Xinomavro from the Yianakohori vineyard defines this bottling, where limestone-rich soils and a cool Macedonian climate produce a structural profile often compared to Barolo. By selecting fruit from specific blocks with southern exposure, Kir-Yianni creates a wine that balances aggressive tannins with high natural acidity.
parsed.wine_summary:
Ramnista is a benchmark for Naoussa, representing the modern evolution of the Xinomavro grape. Kir-Yianni, founded by Yiannis Boutaris, focuses on taming the variety's notoriously fierce phenolic structure through precise vineyard management and aging in French and American oak. This 100% Xinomavro is sourced from the estate's undulating hills, where the variation in slope and soil creates a wine of high aromatic complexity.

The wine matters because it proves that Greek indigenous varieties can produce long-lived, site-specific reds that compete with the great nebbiolo-based wines of the world. While many Naoussa producers struggled with consistency in the past, the recurring gold and silver medals from TEXSOM across the 2011-2015 vintages confirm that Ramnista is a reliable standard-bearer for the appellation.
parsed.terroir_expression: The Naoussa appellation is characterized by a Mediterranean climate with continental influences, but Ramnista specifically benefits from the clay-limestone soils of the Yianakohori estate. This calcium-rich geology contributes to the wine's 'salty' mineral finish and helps regulate the vine's water intake, while the 280-330m altitude ensures cool nights that preserve malic acid. The result is a palate defined by sun-dried tomato and olive tapenade notes, a direct sensory link to the scrubby, herbal landscape of northern Greece.
parsed.vinification_summary: Winemaking centers on managing Xinomavro’s high tannin—the polyphenolic compounds found in grape skins and seeds that provide grip—through a 12-to-15-month aging period in 225-liter and 500-liter oak barrels. The use of larger formats and 25% new wood prevents the oak from masking the grape's delicate floral and spice aromas. Malolactic fermentation, the process of converting sharp malic acid into softer lactic acid, is fully completed to round out the wine's naturally high-strung acidity.
parsed.food_pairing: Slow-roasted lamb shoulder with rosemary and garlic works because the wine's high acidity cuts through the fat while the tannins bind to the protein. For a casual pairing, try a lamb gyro with extra tzatziki; the cucumber and garlic in the sauce highlight the wine's herbal undertones. Smoked brisket with a vinegar-based North Carolina BBQ sauce provides a sharp counterpoint to the wine's dried fruit notes. In a fine dining setting, wild mushroom risotto with truffle oil complements the savory, earthy development found in older vintages like the 2013.
parsed.comparable_wines: Produttori del Barbaresco Torre — shares the same translucent color, high acidity, and firm tannic spine found in Xinomavro. Vietti Perbacco Nebbiolo delle Langhe — offers a similar balance of red fruit and savory earthiness at a near-identical price point. Domaine Sigalas Mavrotragano — another Greek high-acid red that emphasizes volcanic-style minerality and structural longevity.
parsed.style_profile: Medium-bodied dry red with high acidity, assertive tannins, and savory tomato-leaf notes
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink now after decanting for two hours, or cellar for another 5-8 years to allow the tannins to soften into a silky texture.
parsed.value_assessment: $29.46 is an aggressive price for a wine that consistently earns gold medals and ages like a top-tier Piemontese red. It competes directly with entry-level Langhe Nebbiolo or mid-range Rioja Reserva, but offers significantly more structural depth and site-specificity than most $30 domestic Pinot Noirs. It is an essential purchase for collectors building a cellar on a budget.
parsed.market_position: Ramnista occupies the 'sommelier's secret' niche on restaurant lists, frequently appearing in trendy Mediterranean spots and wine bars focused on indigenous varieties. While it hasn't reached the mainstream recognition of Napa Cabernet, it is a staple for retail shops that cater to curious drinkers looking for high-acid, food-friendly alternatives to Pinot Noir. It is a 'buy by the case' wine for those who value structure over fruit-forward ripeness.
parsed.insider_take: The tradeoff with Ramnista is its uncompromising acidity; if you prefer plush, jammy reds like Zinfandel, you will find this wine painfully austere. It is a wine for the patient drinker who understands that Xinomavro is meant to be a savory experience rather than a fruit bomb. Skip this if you aren't serving it with food, as the tannins require protein to show their best side.
